newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP shares fall, retest A$16 level.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP shares fall, retest A$16 level.

text.p: Shares in market bellwether, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, slid through the A$16.00 mark in Tuesday afternoon trade, weighed down by soft copper prices and nervousness ahead of its first quarter results, due Friday.
After reaching an intra-day low of A$15.95, the market leader recovered some ground to close at A$16.00, down 48 cents from Monday's close on turnover of 4.56 million shares.
"The sellers have taken charge in the afternoon," said a Sydney-based dealer. He said a combination of weakening commodity prices and concern over profit results had seen investors cut positions.
"No-one is keen to buy ahead of the results and the copper price isn't helping either."
Other players agreed, adding that recent volatility had suggested players were still setting positions.
"Softer commodities prices isn't helping them and given the volatility of late, there is still some setting of positions ahead of the results," said dealer Philip Toop of Lance Jones.

Some brokers, though, cautioned about reading too much into the stock's steepening fall in the afternoon session, noting that the overall market had itself softened further and pointed to BHP's role as a proxy for the broader Australian market.
"There may be some anticipation of the Dow coming off tonight after its run but the whole market has come off in the afternoon," said senior dealer at Nevitts Ltd, Jum Tredenick.
"Also, the stock has had a good run up since hitting its lows last week."

Last week, BHP shares touched a 28 month low of A$15.58, following profit downgrades by stockbroking analysts and bearish comments by managing director John Prescott on the future of the copper price and its steel operations.
Earlier today, the company said eight month output from its 57.5 percent owned Escondida copper mine in Chile was up 82 percent on 1995, reaching 561,000 tonnes.
